# Anthropic OAuth path vs API-key path

**Question.** What is actually different between calling Anthropic with a Claude subscription OAuth token (`sk-ant-oat…`, as `tailnet-microservices` does) and with a Console API key (`sk-ant-api…`), why do the harnesses I use pick one or the other, and what does that mean for the proxy's recurring "reset the token" outage?

## 1. The wire contract

Both paths `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`. The differences:

| | API key | Subscription OAuth |
|---|---|---|
| Auth | `x-api-key` | `Authorization: Bearer` + `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` **[quoted]** promptfoo `src/providers/anthropic/claudeCodeAuth.ts:36-46`; pi `packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts:924-946` |
| Identity gate | none | `user-agent: claude-cli/…` else **401** **[quoted]** promptfoo `claudeCodeAuth.ts:53-59`: "Anthropic's API gates OAuth tokens to the Claude Code app identity, so requests that use a different user-agent fail with 401" |
| System prompt | free | first `system` block must be exactly `You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude.` else **400** **[quoted]** promptfoo `claudeCodeAuth.ts:24-31` ("As of 2025-Q4 … Re-verify"); pi `anthropic-messages.ts:1009-1015` ("we MUST include Claude Code identity") |
| Extra betas | feature betas only | `claude-code-20250219` (tool surface) **[quoted]** promptfoo, pi, openclaw `extensions/anthropic/stream-wrappers.ts:35-43` |
| Endpoints | full API | `/v1/messages` only **[quoted]** promptfoo `generic.ts:175-180` |
| Disabled features | — | fast mode / service tier / server-side compaction **[quoted]** openclaw `stream-wrappers.ts:200-205`, openclaw docs |
| Limits | RPM/TPM tiers | rolling 5-hour plan window; 429 body "usage limit for your plan" **[quoted]** `specs/anthropic-oauth-gateway.md:306-316` (our classifier) |
| Billing | per token | plan usage, or "extra usage" per token — see §3 |
| Official docs | yes | **none.** Every row above is reverse-engineered from Claude Code's wire traffic (cedws gist; our `docs/audits/header-provenance.md`; promptfoo's and PR #73's MITM tests) **[observed]** |

Token/credential mechanics, all **[quoted]** unless noted:
- Keychain entry `Claude Code-credentials` → `claudeAiOauth: {accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt(ms), subscriptionType}` (promptfoo `claudeCodeAuth.ts`; our `docs/runbook/accounts.md:95`).
- PKCE: `AUTHORIZE_URL https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize` (pi) / `https://claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize` (PR #73), `TOKEN_URL https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token`, client id `9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e` (base64-obfuscated in both pi and PR #73), redirect `http://localhost:53692/callback`, scopes `org:create_api_key user:profile user:inference user:sessions:claude_code user:mcp_servers user:file_upload`.
- Access token ≈ 8 h **[observed]**: our background refresh succeeded every ~7h45m, 2026-07-22 → 2026-08-01.
- Refresh token is **rotated on every refresh and single-lineage** **[quoted]** CodexBar `ClaudeOAuthCredentials.swift:742-743` "Claude Code rotates refresh tokens"; openclaw `docs/concepts/oauth.md:41-46` "The token sink … Some providers invalidate the previous refresh token when a new one is issued … log in via OpenClaw *and* via Claude Code / Codex CLI, and one of them randomly gets logged out later."
- Refresh token lifetime: **~6 weeks [observed, n=1]** — loaded ~2026-06-20, `invalid_grant / "Refresh token expired"` at 2026-08-01 18:36Z. June's failure had a different description, `"Refresh token not found or invalid"`. No source states a numeric TTL.

## 2. Anthropic's policy, dated

All **[quoted]**, official unless marked.
- **2026-01** enforcement begins; OpenCode drops subscription support "citing anthropic legal requests" (The Register, 2026-02-20, https://www.theregister.com/2026/02/20/anthropic_clarifies_ban_third_party_claude_access/).
- **2026-02-20** Anthropic wording: "Using OAuth tokens obtained through Claude Free, Pro, or Max accounts in any other product, tool, or service — including the Agent SDK — is not permitted and constitutes a violation of the Consumer Terms of Service." Engineer (Thariq Shihipar): third-party harnesses "generate unusual traffic patterns without any of the usual telemetry that the Claude Code harness provides."
- **2026-04-04** subscriptions stop covering third-party tools (Boris Cherny via VentureBeat): "our subscriptions weren't built for the usage patterns of these third-party tools."
- **2026-05-13** partial reinstatement: monthly **Agent SDK credits** billed at API rates — Pro $20 / Max 5x $100 / Max 20x $200 — then pay-as-you-go (VentureBeat). This is the sanctioned route; it does not bless spoofing Claude Code headers.
- **Current** https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance: "OAuth authentication is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications … developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens … Anthropic reserves the right to take measures to enforce these restrictions and may do so without prior notice."
- Community, not official: openclaw `docs/concepts/oauth.md:16-20` "Anthropic staff told us this usage is allowed again, so OpenClaw treats Claude CLI reuse and `claude -p` usage as sanctioned … unless Anthropic publishes a new policy. For Anthropic in production, API key auth is still the safer recommended path."

## 3. "Plan usage" vs "extra usage" — what is and isn't known

- pi warns its own users **[quoted]** `packages/coding-agent/docs/providers.md:35`: "Anthropic subscription auth is active. Third-party harness usage draws from extra usage and is billed per token, not your Claude plan limits."
- openclaw documents the symptom **[quoted]** `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md:151`: `HTTP 429: rate_limit_error: Extra usage is required for long context requests`.
- Our repo's framing **[quoted]** `docs/runbook/clients.md`: the Pi sanitizer exists "because Anthropic's Max-plan classifier treats that hint as extra-usage traffic even with Claude Code attribution"; the observed client error is `400 You're out of extra usage`.
- **[unverified]** That a server-side "classifier" keyed on headers/system-prompt decides plan-vs-extra is *our own hypothesis*, supported by one before/after curl in `docs/audits/header-provenance.md` (2026-05-05: adding `x-anthropic-billing-header` flipped a failing request to success). It has never been measured across time or clients. See §7 — the data to measure it does not currently exist.

## 4. How each project positions itself

| Project | Path | Refresh ownership | Stated reason / caveat |
|---|---|---|---|
| **simmer-sdk** (`2389-research`) | API key only (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `AsyncAnthropic`) | n/a | **[observed]** zero hits for `oauth\|subscription\|sk-ant-oat\|setup-token\|login` in source, docs, and the commit messages on `dispatch.py`/`api_agent.py`. Issues/PRs/discussions **not** checked. The 2026-04-12 commit `109820ae` that made `api` dispatch default over `cli` (Claude Agent SDK subprocess) says **[quoted]**: "No Node.js, no CLI spawn, no zombie processes. Standard async HTTP via the Anthropic Python SDK." It does not mention auth either way. |
| **promptfoo** | both; API key default, OAuth via `apiKeyRequired: false` | reads keychain, never refreshes ("run `claude /login`") | **[quoted]** `site/docs/providers/anthropic.md:30` "reuse [your Claude Code session's] OAuth credential instead of creating a separate Anthropic Console API key"; billing hedged: "expected to count against your Claude subscription … check Anthropic's documentation." Meta/Bedrock providers refuse to forward the OAuth token. |
| **pi** (`badlogic/pi-mono`) | both; own PKCE with Claude Code client id | refreshes itself, 5 min early | "Stealth mode: Mimic Claude Code's tool naming exactly" **[quoted]** `anthropic-messages.ts:76-100`; extra-usage warning (§3). No ToS statement. |
| **openclaw** | API key, CLI reuse via Agent SDK, or pasted `claude setup-token` | **none** — "never reads, persists, refreshes, selects, or forwards the native login tokens. Claude owns the login and token refresh lifecycle." **[quoted]** `docs/providers/anthropic.md`; keychain reader retired (`provider-auth-claude-compat.ts:12`) | "For long-lived gateway hosts, an Anthropic API key is still the most predictable choice" **[quoted]** `docs/gateway/authentication.md:48` |
| **CodexBar** (`steipete`) | OAuth token for `/api/oauth/usage` only, never inference | tri-state ownership; CLI-owned chains delegated to `claude` CLI; "never rotate a chain we cannot prove we own" **[quoted]** `ClaudeOAuthCredentials.swift:769-771` | purely technical rationale; `invalid_grant` → terminal, keyed to refresh-token hash; transient backoff 5 min → 6 h |
| **amplifier PR #73** (`gszep`, "🏴‍☠️ claude oauth alternative") | adds pi-style OAuth to an API-key-only provider | refreshes itself | **[observed]** open since 2026-07-19, 0 comments, 0 reviews, unmerged; body: "I hope you will find this implementation instructive"; no policy discussion |
| **tailnet-microservices** (ours) | OAuth pool on a PVC, keychain-extracted | refreshes itself; disables on `invalid_grant`; no auto-recovery | design inherited from Loom's mitmproxy capture (vault `Note-Loom-Patterns.md:238-270`); no written rationale for OAuth-over-API exists in the repo |
| **prompting-eval-workbench** (ours) | API-shaped client (`agent_dispatch="api"`, `apiKeyRequired: false`) **through the OAuth proxy** | proxy's | **[quoted]** `evals/simmer/simmer-pivot-assumptions…json` A3+A4 "ALL GREEN through proxy … AsyncAnthropic() constructs with NO key"; the only API-key concern recorded was CI (GitHub Actions had no secrets; "OAuth-proxied route" deferred as a separate design, `docs/gh-agentic-workflows/eval-scaffold-review.md:132-136`) |

## 5. What this means for the proxy

1. **The ~6-week re-auth is structural [inferred from §1 + §4].** The refresh chain is single-lineage and the proxy holds a copy extracted from a keychain that Claude Code also refreshes. Two projects (openclaw, CodexBar) refuse to own that chain for this exact reason. Skip-on-disabled + alerting make the outage visible; only "let the CLI own the chain and re-pull from it" or a sanctioned credential removes it.
2. **The sanctioned alternative exists** since 2026-05-13 (Agent SDK credit at API rates). It is what openclaw's and pi's docs point at for production.
3. **PKCE-for-third-parties status is dated 2026-02-17** (CC 2.1.44) and untested since. See §6.

## 6. Corrections to earlier over-claims (2026-08-26 session)

- ~~"This is why your PKCE flow broke on 2026-02-17"~~ → **[unverified]**. The recorded error was `POST /v1/oauth/{session_id}/authorize → 400 "Invalid request format"` (first seen ~2026-02-12). Date proximity to the Feb-2026 policy enforcement is the only link; a request-shape mismatch is equally consistent. Nobody has retested.
- ~~"simmer-sdk never considered OAuth"~~ → **no OAuth consideration is recorded in the repository contents.** Issues/PRs/discussions not checked.
- ~~"The reason was plumbing, not auth"~~ → the commit's stated motivation is subprocess elimination; **auth is not mentioned either way**. "Plumbing" was my paraphrase; "not auth" had no basis.
- ~~"Anthropic's classifier" as the cause of extra-usage billing~~ → our repo's hypothesis plus pi's warning plus one curl. **No long-term study was run.** See §7.

## 7. What changes about the "study" question

A proper answer to "is a classifier billing us as extra usage, and when" needs a time series of upstream non-2xx responses with their error bodies, per client, over weeks. **That data does not exist anywhere as of 2026-08-26:**

- **Pod logs — gone.** The `rollout restart` used for the 2026-08-26 re-auth replaced pod `anthropic-oauth-proxy-6d645954c8-jp6tv` and its 35 days of logs (`kubectl logs > file` was not taken first — my error). radar found no Loki/Vector/Alloy/Promtail in the cluster.
- **netdata — has nothing for this service [observed via `netdata_cloud_mcp`].** Room `mothership-k8s` (space `Crashoverride6 space`), node `talos-0db-np3`: `search_metrics` finds no `pool_account_status`, `pool_token_refreshes_total`, `proxy_upstream_errors_total`, and no k8s cgroup/pod contexts (only `prometheus.haproxy.*`). The node advertises `systemd-journal` and `otel-logs` functions, but both return `No log entries found` even unfiltered over 24 h — registered, not ingesting.
- **Even with retention the data would be unclassifiable.** The proxy logs an upstream 400 as `request completed (transient error) status 400` with **no body** (e.g. 2026-08-01T18:20:27Z, cause unknown).

Prerequisites before the study can be *done* (not started here; flagged only):

1. Scrape the proxy's `:9090/metrics` into netdata (Prometheus collector / whatever the k8s-netdata deployment uses) → `pool_account_status{status="disabled"} > 0` becomes a real alert; refresh failures become a series.
2. Ship container logs to the `otel-logs` receiver that is already registered on the Talos nodes.
3. Change the proxy to log the upstream error `type` and message on every non-2xx.
4. Then, and only then: count `extra usage` responses over time by client (Pi vs raw curl vs Claude Code), with and without the sanitizer/billing header, to test the classifier hypothesis.

for "PKCE-for-third-parties status is dated 2026-02-17** (CC 2.1.44) and untested since" what does untested mean here?

It means: nobody has re-run the PKCE flow against Anthropic's authorize endpoint since Feb 17. Specifically —

**What was tested, once:** on 2026-02-17 the constants were aligned to CC CLI v2.1.44 (`52a8fee`), then Steps 1–3 in `accounts.md` were run: `init-oauth` → open the consent page → click Authorize. The browser's `POST /v1/oauth/{session_id}/authorize` returned `400 "Invalid request format"`, in normal and incognito sessions. That's recorded in `d01eb8a`.

**What "untested since" is based on:** the only evidence I have is *absence* — `git log -i --grep=pkce` shows no commits after Feb 17, `git log -S'blocked by Anthropic'` shows the sentence was carried forward verbatim through two doc reorgs (Apr 28, Jul 2), and Entire search turned up no later session on the topic. So the claim is really "no retest is *recorded* in the repo or checkpoints." If you ran it by hand and didn't commit anything, I wouldn't know.

**Why it matters that it's stale, concretely:** three things have moved since the one test —
1. The authorize endpoint pi uses is `https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize`; PR #73 (Jul 2026) uses `https://claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize`. Ours (`crates/anthropic-auth`) still points wherever it did in February — I haven't checked which, and if it's the old host that alone could produce a 400.
2. The scope set grew: pi and PR #73 send `user:sessions:claude_code user:mcp_servers user:file_upload`; our Feb fix added `user:mcp_servers` only.
3. Anthropic's policy changed twice (Apr 4 cutoff, May 13 partial reinstatement), so whatever the server was enforcing in February may not be what it enforces now — in either direction.

So "untested" isn't a claim that it's broken or that it works; it's that the "blocked" label rests on one observation made against parameters that are now six months and three policy events old. Retesting is cheap: `init-oauth` → authorize → `complete-oauth`, ~2 minutes. If it succeeds, PKCE gives the proxy its own refresh-token lineage (no shared keychain chain), which is the structural fix for the 6-week outage.

Found the deltas. pi's authorize request has four things ours doesn't, and the 10-minute PKCE state from our `init-oauth` is still live, so I can hand-build variants on the same `code_challenge`/`state` — if one renders the consent page and you authorize, `complete-oauth` still works (for A and B).

| | ours | pi |
|---|---|---|
| `code=true` param | missing | present |
| scopes | 4 | + `org:create_api_key`, `user:file_upload` |
| `redirect_uri` | `https://platform.claude.com/oauth/code/callback` | `http://localhost:53692/callback` |
| `state` | account id | random verifier |

Try these in order; stop at the first that shows a consent page instead of "Invalid request format":

**A — add `code=true` only** (exchange still valid):
```
https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize?code=true&client_id=9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fplatform.claude.com%2Foauth%2Fcode%2Fcallback&response_type=code&scope=user%3Aprofile%20user%3Ainference%20user%3Asessions%3Aclaude_code%20user%3Amcp_servers&REDACTED&code_challenge_method=S256&state=claude-max-1787728438
```

**B — A + pi's full scope set** (exchange still valid):
```
https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize?code=true&client_id=9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fplatform.claude.com%2Foauth%2Fcode%2Fcallback&response_type=code&scope=org%3Acreate_api_key%20user%3Aprofile%20user%3Ainference%20user%3Asessions%3Aclaude_code%20user%3Amcp_servers%20user%3Afile_upload&REDACTED&code_challenge_method=S256&state=claude-max-1787728438
```

**C — pi's exact shape incl. localhost redirect** (diagnostic only — the token exchange would fail on redirect mismatch, but if *this* one renders consent, the redirect URI is the gate):
```
https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize?code=true&client_id=9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A53692%2Fcallback&scope=org%3Acreate_api_key%20user%3Aprofile%20user%3Ainference%20user%3Asessions%3Aclaude_code%20user%3Amcp_servers%20user%3Afile_upload&REDACTED&code_challenge_method=S256&state=claude-max-1787728438
```

If A or B gives you a `code#state` after Authorize, paste it and I'll complete the flow. If all three fail identically, that's real evidence for a server-side gate on the client rather than request shape.

Confirmed against the right source now. `earendil-works/pi` main (`packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/anthropic.ts:30-36, 248-252`) and your installed pi **0.84.3** bundle (`dist/bundle/chunks/anthropic.js`) both send exactly what the mirror showed:

- scopes `org:create_api_key user:profile user:inference user:sessions:claude_code user:mcp_servers user:file_upload`
- token endpoint `https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token` (same as ours)

Two dated facts from pi's changelog worth noting: Anthropic OAuth was pulled in 0.40.1 (2026-01-09, "Use API keys instead") and restored in 0.41.0 the same day; and 0.58.2 (2026-03-15) "Fixed Anthropic OAuth manual login and token refresh by using the localhost callback URI" — i.e. pi had a period where a non-localhost redirect broke, which is the delta between our config and theirs. So the badlogic mirror was stale for the repo name, not for these params, and the three test URLs I gave you stand as-is. The PKCE state from `init-oauth` is still live for a few more minutes — try **A**, then **B**, then **C**; if C is the first to render a consent page, the `redirect_uri` is what's being rejected and the fix is a one-line constant change in `crates/anthropic-auth/src/constants.rs:11` plus a local callback listener (or manual paste) in the admin flow.

That's a real result, and it changes the picture:

- **Original URL → fails on page load.** Adding `code=true` fixes that — all three variants rendered the consent page. That's a confirmed request-shape bug on our side.
- **Consent → Authorize → "Invalid request format"** for A, B, and C alike — and C is byte-for-byte pi's current shape *except one parameter*: **`state`**. Pi (and Claude Code) send the PKCE verifier as `state` — a 43-char base64url string. We send `claude-max-1787728438`. "Invalid request format" is a schema-validation message, and a short hyphenated `state` is now the only remaining delta.

**D:**
```
https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize?code=true&client_id=9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A53692%2Fcallback&scope=org%3Acreate_api_key%20user%3Aprofile%20user%3Ainference%20user%3Asessions%3Aclaude_code%20user%3Amcp_servers%20user%3Afile_upload&REDACTED&code_challenge_method=S256&REDACTED
```

What to expect:
- **If Authorize succeeds**, the browser will try `http://localhost:53692/callback?code=…&state=…` and fail to load (nothing listening) — that's fine; the URL bar will contain the code. Tell me it redirected (don't paste the code — it's not usable with our stored verifier anyway). That would nail it: the gate is the `state` format, and the proxy fix is (1) `code=true`, (2) send a random base64url `state` and map it to the account id server-side — two small changes in `admin.rs`/`constants.rs`.
- **If it fails identically**, then the remaining differences between D and a working pi login are things I can't reproduce by URL alone (a real listener, or the server keying on something beyond the query string), and "server-side gate" becomes the better-supported explanation.

As a control, `pi` is installed here (0.84.3) — running `/login anthropic` in it would tell us whether pi's own flow works for your account today, which is the ground truth the whole comparison rests on.
http://localhost:53692/callback?code= with longass code i redacted

That settles it. **The PKCE flow is not blocked by Anthropic — it was our request shape.** Two bugs:

1. Missing `code=true` → the authorize page itself rejects the request (today's first screenshot).
2. `state` = the account id (`claude-max-…`) → consent renders, but the Authorize POST returns "Invalid request format". A 43-char base64url `state` (what pi and Claude Code send — the PKCE verifier) goes through.

C and D differed *only* in `state`, so that's isolated. The Feb-17 "Q13-gate" investigation aligned client id, redirect, scopes, and S256, but never the `state` format — so "platform constraint" was wrong for six months. Note the redirect didn't matter: `https://platform.claude.com/oauth/code/callback` (A/B) rendered consent just like localhost did, so the proxy can keep its manual-paste flow.

Updating the docs to reflect this now, since the runbook and vault note both still carry the disproven claim.

# Tailnet Microservices — Agent Guidelines

## Overview

Tailnet Microservices is a Rust workspace that produces one deployable binary, `anthropic-oauth-proxy`. The service accepts unauthenticated tailnet requests, manages Claude Max OAuth credentials, selects accounts from a round-robin pool with quota failover, rewrites requests to match the required Anthropic and Claude Code contracts, and streams upstream responses back to clients.

The Tailscale Operator owns tailnet identity and ingress. The service remains a plain Kubernetes workload with ClusterIP backends. OAuth credentials persist on a PVC.

## Non-negotiable boundaries

- **Do not modify anything in `mothership-gitops`.** ArgoCD syncs this repository at wave 8.
- Do not manually deploy, push commits, or change external infrastructure unless the task explicitly requires it.
- Never log, trace, snapshot, commit, or return OAuth access tokens or refresh tokens.
- Preserve restrictive credential-file permissions and atomic credential writes.
- In OAuth mode, client `Authorization` and `x-api-key` headers must never reach Anthropic.
- Do not expose the admin listener through the Tailscale Ingress or a public Service. The runbook accesses it through `kubectl port-forward`.
- Keep logs, metrics, and traces content-free: do not record prompts, request or response bodies, credentials, or authorization headers.

## Architecture and ownership

The workspace contains four libraries and one binary:

```text
crates/
  common/           Shared configuration/error support
  provider/         Provider trait, error classification, passthrough provider
  anthropic-auth/   OAuth PKCE, token exchange/refresh, credential persistence
  anthropic-pool/   Account selection, cooldown, disabling, quota handling, refresh
services/
  oauth-proxy/      Axum service, admin API, proxy transaction loop, telemetry
specs/              Current and historical design specifications
k8s/                Deployment, Services, Ingress, PVC, and generated configuration
docs/runbook/       Current operational procedures
docs/audits/        Timestamped investigations and compatibility evidence
```

Respect these ownership boundaries:

- Keep generic forwarding, retry, streaming, and response behavior in `services/oauth-proxy/src/proxy.rs`.
- Keep provider-specific authentication and request mutation behind `provider::Provider`.
- Keep token exchange and credential durability in `anthropic-auth`.
- Keep account selection and account-state transitions in `anthropic-pool`.
- Keep process assembly and listener startup in `main.rs`; do not put reusable domain logic there.
- Search for an existing abstraction before adding helpers or plumbing state across layers.
- Keep crate API surfaces small. Default modules, types, and helpers to private unless another crate genuinely requires them.

The most load-bearing surfaces are `proxy.rs::proxy_request`, `provider_impl.rs`, the pool and refresh state machines, credential persistence, and the `k8s/`/CI deployment handoff. Changes there require focused review beyond compilation success.

## Specification and documentation authority

- Read `specs/README.md` before treating an individual spec as current. Several specs are historical or superseded.
- Historical specs are design evidence, not current requirements.
- Use `docs/runbook/README.md` as the entry point for current operator procedures.
- Treat audits and commit messages as timestamped claims. Open the referenced implementation and tests before acting on them.
- When intent matters, inspect the introducing or correcting Git diff.
- Update the governing current spec or runbook when behavior or operations change.

A document that points to source provides a route to evidence, not verification. Confidence should rise only with the strongest surface actually checked: source and deterministic tests for local behavior; header capture for Claude Code wire parity; Kubernetes, tailnet, and Phoenix checks for live behavior.

## Development workflow

Use the tasks in `mise.toml` as the canonical tool and command interface. Mise provisions Rust, Clippy, rustfmt, cargo-audit, cargo-zigbuild, kubeconform, and header-capture tooling.

```bash
mise run fmt             # Format source
mise run fmt:check       # Check formatting without mutation
mise run lint            # Clippy, warnings denied
mise run build           # Debug workspace build
mise run test            # Workspace tests
mise run check           # fmt check -> lint -> build -> test
mise run ci              # check + audit + release size + Kubernetes validation
```

Focused Rust commands are appropriate during development:

```bash
cargo test -p provider
cargo test -p anthropic-auth
cargo test -p anthropic-pool
cargo test -p oauth-proxy
cargo test -p oauth-proxy test_name
```

Validation escalation:

- For ordinary source changes, run focused tests while iterating and `mise run check` before finalizing.
- For dependency, release, Docker, or Kubernetes changes, run `mise run ci`.
- For cross-compilation work, use `mise run build:cross-x86` and/or `mise run build:cross-arm64`.
- `mise run headers:capture` is a vendor-wire investigation requiring mitmproxy and a current Claude Code client.
- `mise run live:validate` is read-only but requires cluster, tailnet, Pi, and Phoenix access. Run it only when the task requires live evidence and those surfaces are available.
- Do not claim live deployment health, telemetry ingestion, or current Claude Code parity from deterministic source checks alone.

Rust builds can wait on Cargo locks. Treat slow progress as normal; do not kill compiler or test processes solely because they are quiet.

## Rust and API conventions

- Follow rustfmt and Clippy with warnings denied.
- Prefer exhaustive `match` statements for account, lifecycle, and error state machines. Avoid wildcard arms that hide newly added variants.
- Prefer self-documenting API shapes over positional boolean or ambiguous `Option` parameters. Use enums, newtypes, builders, or named methods where they improve call sites.
- New traits must document their role, invariants, and implementation contract.
- Preserve object safety where dynamic providers require `Arc<dyn Provider>`; do not mechanically replace boxed futures with an incompatible trait shape.
- Prefer private modules and explicit exports.
- Avoid one-off abstractions that merely move code. Extract cohesive responsibilities with their tests and documentation.
- Instrument async work at the owning function or method when practical. Check for existing instrumentation before adding another span.
- Avoid unrelated style churn while making behavioral changes.

## Testing rules

- Behavior changes require tests at the layer that owns the behavior.
- Proxy retry, failover, streaming, header, and request-mutation changes require service-level integration coverage.
- Pool selection, cooldown, disabling, and refresh classification belong in `anthropic-pool` tests.
- PKCE, token classification, and credential persistence belong in `anthropic-auth` tests.
- Use local mock HTTP servers. Do not add tests that contact Anthropic, a live cluster, tailnet services, or operator infrastructure.
- Prefer asserting complete responses or state objects over many independent field assertions when the complete value is stable and meaningful.
- Do not add tests that only restate static constants. Test the behavior those constants produce.
- Avoid mutating process-wide environment in tests; inject configuration or dependencies where practical.
- When introducing a substantial new test module, prefer a sibling `*_tests.rs` file instead of further growing an inline implementation test module. Do not move existing tests solely for style conformity.
- Unit and integration tests can establish construction and behavior, but they cannot establish current vendor-wire parity.

## Compatibility surfaces

Before changing public behavior, search callers, tests, current specs, and runbooks for these contracts:

- HTTP request/response semantics, hop-by-hop header handling, body limits, retries, and SSE streaming.
- Configuration TOML and persisted credential formats.
- Admin API, `/health`, and Prometheus metric names and labels.
- OpenTelemetry span names, status, and attributes.
- Kubernetes resource names, ports, labels, PVC paths, ingress routing, and immutable image tags.
- Claude Code identity headers, beta flags, billing attribution, and system-prompt mutation.

Claude Code compatibility is empirical and perishable. Before changing `REQUIRED_BETA_FLAGS`, `USER_AGENT`, `X_APP`, `ANTHROPIC_BILLING_HEADER`, or system-prompt rewriting, read the provenance audits, inspect `provider_impl.rs` and its tests, and use `mise run headers:capture` when claiming parity with a current release.

Preserve streaming semantics: the initial upstream response has a timeout, while an established response stream uses an idle timeout. Do not replace this with a wall-clock timeout over the complete SSE response.

Preserve observability on every return path. Request counters, error counters, in-flight accounting, duration metrics, and span finalization must remain consistent across success, retry, failover, timeout, and early-error branches.

## Change-size and module guidance

Prefer focused, reviewable changes. For non-mechanical work, treat roughly 500 changed lines as a review trigger and 800 changed lines as a strong signal to split the work into coherent stages. Base staging on actual dependencies and affected call sites, not arbitrary file boundaries.

Several modules are already large. Do not add substantial new behavior to `main.rs`, `proxy.rs`, `admin.rs`, `config.rs`, `provider_impl.rs`, or `pool.rs` without first considering whether a cohesive module should own it. Do not split code merely to satisfy a line count; keep invariants, tests, and module documentation close to their implementation.

## Final review checklist

Before finalizing, verify:

- The change respects crate ownership and reuses existing abstractions.
- Credentials and request content cannot leak through logs, errors, metrics, traces, fixtures, or snapshots.
- Retry and failover counts have not combined into unintended multiplicative attempts.
- Streaming behavior and idle-timeout semantics remain correct.
- Public configuration, admin, health, metrics, telemetry, and Kubernetes contracts were considered.
- Tests are deterministic, local, and cover the owning layer.
- Current documentation was updated without treating historical material as authoritative.
- The narrowest sufficient validation was run, and any unverified live behavior is reported explicitly.

Done. Six commits on `main`, unpushed, undeployed; tree clean except your two pre-existing unrelated files.

**Result:** the admin PKCE flow works end to end on the patched code — `init-oauth` → browser Authorize → `complete-oauth` `{"status":"added"}` → pool `healthy` → live `/v1/messages` → `"ok"`. Credential landed as `sk-ant-oat0…` (8 h access) + `sk-ant-ort0…` (refresh). The local proxy is stopped and its credential file shredded; the proxy log contained no tokens.

**It was three bugs, not two**, and none of them were policy:
1. no `code=true` → authorize page fails on load
2. `state` = account id → Authorize POST rejects
3. `code_verifier` 171 chars (RFC 7636 max 128) → token endpoint rejects — only reachable after 1 and 2 were fixed, which is why February never saw it

**Commits**
| | |
|---|---|
| `b883966` | fix(auth): `code=true` + random 43-char `state`, PKCE map keyed by state, `state` echoed to token endpoint, tests |
| `18c095a` | docs(runbook): refresh-token lifetime, disabled-account known issues, PKCE reclassified |
| `20a265c` | docs(agents): test-first rule; radar / netdata-via-executor / log-capture-before-restart |
| `4bdb8e7` | chore(lint): the two pre-existing clippy 1.94 lints in `main.rs` — `mise run check` is clean again |
| `391a62a` | fix(auth): verifier 32 bytes — test flipped first, red, then fixed |
| `a8be778` | docs(runbook): PKCE marked fixed + verified, pending deploy; `complete-oauth` now `{"code":"CODE#STATE"}` |

Vault note §5.3 and §6 updated to match.

**Open, your call:** deploy (push → CI image → `deploy:` tag bump → ArgoCD), then re-provision `claude-max-local` via PKCE so the proxy owns its own refresh lineage instead of sharing your keychain's; optionally bump `PKCE_EXPIRY_SECS` from 10 min (it bit us once today); and the still-untouched `refresh_cycle` skip-on-`Disabled` guard.

### opentelemetry_sdk has unbounded memory allocation in W3C Baggage propagation
[CVE-2026-48504](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48504) / [GHSA-w9wp-h8wv-79jx](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-w9wp-h8wv-79jx)
<details>
<summary>More information</summary>
#### Details
##### Summary
`BaggagePropagator::extract_with_context` in `opentelemetry_sdk` did not enforce the W3C Baggage size limits before parsing an inbound `baggage` header. A large attacker-controlled header could cause unnecessary CPU work and short-lived heap allocations while parsing entries that would later be discarded by the SDK's baggage storage limits.
The SDK now applies limits aligned with the W3C Baggage limits:
  - 64 list-members
  - 8192 bytes total
##### Impact
Services that accept untrusted inbound propagation headers may experience increased per-request resource usage when processing oversized `baggage` headers. This can contribute to denial-of-service risk, especially when application or transport-level header limits are absent or configured above the W3C Baggage limits.
 
The impact is limited to availability. This issue does not expose telemetry data, modify telemetry data, or allow code execution.
##### Patches
Upgrade `opentelemetry_sdk` to version `0.32.1` or later.
Version `0.32.1` rejects `baggage` header values larger than 8192 bytes and limits extraction to the first 64 list-members.
  ## Workarounds
If upgrading immediately is not possible, reject or limit inbound `baggage` headers larger than 8192 bytes before invoking OpenTelemetry propagation extraction. This can be enforced at a proxy, gateway, middleware layer, or custom carrier boundary.
##### Resources
  - W3C Baggage limits: https://www.w3.org/TR/baggage/#limits
  - Related OpenTelemetry Java advisory: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/security/advisories/GHSA-rcgg-9c38-7xpx
  - Related OpenTelemetry Go advisory: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-mh2q-q3fh-2475

Full picture, and the good news first: **nothing has changed in the cluster.**

**Deploy state**
- CI on `3b30262` passed all gates; the bot committed `73b5615 deploy: update image tag to sha-3b30262`.
- ArgoCD's `anthropic-oauth-proxy` Application has **no `syncPolicy.automated`** any more (its history shows automated syncs through `432c586` on 2026-07-03, then nothing). It last reconciled at 08:24Z against `3b30262` — which still carried `sha-4abf487` — and reports `Synced`. On its next reconcile it'll go `OutOfSync` for `73b5615` and sit there. The pod is still `sha-4abf487`, healthy on the keychain re-auth from earlier.
- So the rollout is effectively paused by your own GitOps setup. I have not synced, restarted, or provisioned anything, and won't.

**What the dashboard actually says about dependency state**
- **PR #56 / #55** (`opentelemetry_sdk` 0.31→0.32, CVE-2026-48504, medium, availability-only, W3C baggage parsing): open since **June 30**, and #56 fails Lint/Test/Build with real API breaks (`SdkTracerProvider::tracer` gone, `SpanExporter` trait mismatch, `KeyValue` iterator change). Cause: Renovate bumped `opentelemetry_sdk` alone while the paired `opentelemetry`/`opentelemetry-otlp`/`tracing-opentelemetry` 0.32/0.33 bumps are rate-limited in the separate `rust-observability` group. This needs a coordinated otel 0.32 migration in `telemetry.rs`, not a merge.
- **`cargo audit` passes with that CVE in the tree** because RustSec has no advisory for it (0 vulnerabilities, only the allowed `anyhow` unsoundness warning). GitHub/Dependabot see it; our gate doesn't. That's a real blind spot in the audit gate.
- **PR #51** (Renovate wants to pin the image tag) was manually edited and is now blocked — it conflicts with the CI bot rewriting `newTag` on every push.
- Docker base digests (#52, #54) open since May; ~15 rate-limited updates including `lock-file-maintenance` and the `serde`/`tokio`/observability groups; `actions/checkout` v7 pending approval.

**Where my push fits**
- `3b30262` bumped only `crossbeam-epoch` and `h2` in `Cargo.lock` — the two things RustSec flagged, no code change. It overlaps with what `lock-file-maintenance` would have done; harmless, but it was me routing around Renovate rather than through it, and I didn't look at the dashboard first. Noted.

**Nothing further from me until you say so.** The decisions on the table are yours: whether to sync `73b5615` (the PKCE + verifier fix — proven locally, unrelated to the otel debt), how to tackle the otel 0.32 migration behind #56, and whether the audit gate should also consult the GitHub advisory DB (e.g. `cargo deny` with GHSA, or just merging Dependabot's view). Happy to plan any of those in detail before touching anything.
